blocks.text: For more than a century, Negros Occidental has been known as the Sugar Bowl of the Philippines. The province produces roughly two-thirds of the country’s sugar and has long been an economic anchor of Western Visayas. Sugar has shaped not only the landscape but also the livelihoods of generations of farmers, farmworkers, truck drivers, mill employees, traders, mechanics and small-business operators. Today, however, a troubling question confronts the province and the nation: Is sugar in Negros still sweet? Increasingly, the answer appears to be no.
